body:
### Question

When I have two environments, one for cuda13.0 and one for 12.9, how can I automatically update variables like CUDA_PATH and CUDA_HOME?

Here are the solutions for pixi / conda / mamba. Can uv do something similar automatically?

There's a little-known feature that pixi supports (and conda / mamba too): a package can install a JSON file containing a dictionary of environment variables in $PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT/.pixi/envs/default/etc/conda/env_vars.d/<mypkg>.json. When the environment is activated, these variables are automatically injected. (You need to create the directory and file manually.)
type "D:+AI313.pixienvsdefaultetccondaenv_vars.denv.json"
{
"CUDA_PATH_V13_0": "C:Program FilesNVIDIA GPU Computing ToolkitCUDAv13.0",
"CUDA_HOME": "C:Program FilesNVIDIA GPU Computing ToolkitCUDAv13.0",
"CUDA_PATH": "C:Program FilesNVIDIA GPU Computing ToolkitCUDAv13.0",
"Path": "%CUDA_PATH_V13_0%bin;%CUDA_PATH_V13_0%binx64;%Path%"
}

当我有两个环境时，分别对应 cuda13.0 和 12.9，如何自动修改 CUDA_PATH、CUDA_HOME 这些变量？
以下是 pixi /conda / mamba 的解决方法，uv 可以自动实现类似功能吗？
有一个鲜为人知的特性， pixi 支持（以及 conda / mamba 也支持），软件包可以在$PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT/.pixi/envs/default/etc/conda/env_vars.d/<mypkg>.json 中安装一个包含环境变量字典的 json 文件，在激活环境时，这些变量会自动注入。(该目录和文件需要手工建立)
type "D:\+AI\313\.pixi\envs\default\etc\conda\env_vars.d\env.json"
{
"CUDA_PATH_V13_0": "C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v13.0",
"CUDA_HOME": "C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v13.0",
"CUDA_PATH": "C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v13.0",
"Path": "%CUDA_PATH_V13_0%\\bin;%CUDA_PATH_V13_0%\\bin\\x64;%Path%"
}
